story: Launched in 1973, NASA's Pioneer 11 was built as a backup to explore the outer solar system. It became the first spacecraft to fly by Saturn, discovering its mysterious F-ring and a new moon while surviving a perilous high-speed dive through Jupiter's intense radiation belts. Operating on fading plutonium generators, its final signal was received in late 1995. Today, this silent ghost ship is coasting into interstellar space toward the constellation Aquila, carrying a gold-anodized plaque depicting humanity. It will not pass near the star Lambda Aquilae for another four million years.
angle: Pioneer 11 is coasting in dead silence toward a star in Aquila that it will not reach for four million years.
